versions.localizedDescription: # Theft4 0.3.1 — Performance Improvements **iPhone and iPad · version 0.3.1 · build 142** A performance follow-up to the direct Metal release: less repeated CPU work, cheaper first-use geometry, fewer allocations and better cache behavior. The original Theft4 icon is back. ## What changed - Faster cold geometry conversion and reusable immutable upload backing. - Less work per draw through cached shader metadata, pooled bindings and reusable frame bookkeeping. - Warm pipeline recipes survive cache pressure instead of being cleared together. - Upload VM allocation runs outside the cache mutex; retired sources are cleaned up incrementally and in-flight GPU resources retain their data. - Less CPU busy polling and allocation in multi-object waits. - Native attachment optimizations reduce proven redundant clear/load/store work while preserving the intended image. - Improved compact iPhone launcher layouts. ## Optional Mods menu - **Native Aspect Ratio:** expand the viewport to the launch-window shape, with matching camera/lighting reconstruction, odd-size effects fixes and proportional pause-menu/radar corrections. More visible scenery can increase frame time. - **Custom Time Cycle:** lighting/weather replacement for loose and packed installs. **Credit and thanks to SBerrix** for the custom time cycle. - **God Mode:** player damage/death protection. - **Unlimited Ammo:** reserve ammunition stays available while magazines deplete and reload normally. Select mods before Play; changes take effect on a fresh game launch. The realistic vehicle-handling mod remains planned work and is not included. ## Older devices GPUs without BC-texture support retain the one-time BC-to-ASTC preparation flow: progress, ETA, pause/resume and a saved cache reused on later launches. The tested A12Z uses it; the tested M5 supports BC directly and skips it. The check uses GPU capability rather than an age cutoff. Updating in place retains existing caches. ## Validation and current limits 33 native contracts, 9 mod contracts and 45 real-Metal graphics cases pass, alongside CPU wait sanitizer checks and Release optimization verification. The target remains under 30 ms of total frame work. Remaining first-use spikes, heavy views and device-specific performance are still being improved; this is not a universal locked-30-FPS guarantee. Host fixture savings are not whole-game FPS percentages. Optional mod coverage still needs broader gameplay testing. [Full changelog](https://github.com/KoreanSeats1/Theft4/blob/v0.3.1/CHANGELOG.md) · [0.3.1 release details](https://github.com/KoreanSeats1/Theft4/blob/v0.3.1/docs/RELEASE_0.3.1.md) · [Technical changes and evidence](https://github.com/KoreanSeats1/Theft4/blob/v0.3.1/docs/IOS_MODS.md) ## Install the IPA 1. Download **Theft4-0.3.1-142-ios-arm64.ipa** below. The Source code ZIP is not the IPA. 2. Install with a compatible sideloading tool such as AltStore or SideStore. The IPA is unsigned; your tool must sign it with your Apple account. **Update the existing app in place** to retain game files, saves and prepared textures. Do not delete the app first. 3. For a new install, launch once to create **Files → On My iPhone/iPad → Theft4 → game**, then close the app. 4. Prepare your legally obtained supported Xbox 360 USA retail game: title `545407F2`, media `6AC07221`, base `0.0.0.5`, matching TU8 patch to `0.0.8.5`. A raw ISO or unopened update package is not a prepared installation. 5. Copy the prepared folder's contents into Theft4's existing `game` folder. `default.xex` and `default.xexp` must be at its root, not under `game/game`. 6. Reopen, **Check Game Files**, complete ASTC preparation if required, then Play. Requires ARM64 iOS/iPadOS 26.0 or later. No retail game installation, title update, save, prepared texture cache or developer provisioning profile is included. The credited custom time-cycle resources are included. TestFlight is separate. versions.localizedDescription: # Skate 3 Recompiled v2.7.1 — iOS iOS skipped a release. Everything Android got in v0.2.0 is here, plus two iOS-specific defaults. 24 engine commits and 17 SDK commits since v2.6.3. ## Put any button anywhere Full controller remapping, on the Controls page under **Button Mapping**. Sixteen inputs — the four face buttons, both bumpers, both triggers, both stick clicks, Back, Start and the four D-pad directions — can each be moved to any of the others. Your mapping is saved and survives an update. The sticks themselves are not remapped; Swap Sticks and Invert Camera Y already cover that. ## Three bugs that were costing you frames **Touching the frame-rate row uncapped the game.** One setting's name was a prefix of another's (`..._fps_cap` inside `..._fps_cap_auto`), so changing the Framerate Cap row erased the shipped cap entirely, on every launch after you touched that row. The game then ran the guest loop uncapped. On Android that also meant rendering roughly twice the frames the panel could show and dumping the rest as heat, which is what "runs at 60, drops after a few minutes" was there; iOS presents through FIFO, so the cost here is wasted work rather than heat. **"The frame rate is fine but it feels like slow motion."** Skate 3 advances exactly one refresh period of simulation per rendered frame, however long that frame took, so a 33 ms frame runs the game at half speed. The ceiling that lets a frame advance more than one period (skate3_frame_advance_cap) had been compiled for Switch only — iOS and Android, the two platforms whose frames overrun the period most, never got it. It is compiled in on iOS now. Being straight about this one: the clamp is in and reachable, but raising it was measured as changing nothing on hardware, so treat it as a lever that now exists rather than a fix you are guaranteed to feel. **A profiler was running in every build.** A per-packet GPU timer took two clock reads and two atomic increments on every command packet — around 1.7 million clock reads a second on the busiest thread — whether or not anyone was profiling. It is off unless you ask for it. ## First launch could come up blank Roughly one clean install in ten reached the setup screen with an empty options list and no way forward. Parts of a screen drawn once while their shaders were still compiling were skipped and never came back — and the difficulty prompt is drawn exactly once. Shader compilation now stays synchronous through the cold-boot frontend, so nothing can draw before it is ready. ## New in Settings Eleven new rows, most of them aimed at buying frames back on a phone: - **3D Scene Resolution** — Full / 75% / 67% / 50% / 40%, separate from UI sharpness - **Draw Distance** — now goes down to Quarter and Eighth - **NPC Update Rate** and **World Update Rate** - **Pedestrians & Traffic**, **Movable Props**, **Other Skaters** — stop the world spawning crowds you are not looking at (all three need a restart) - **Vegetation**, **Hair Detail**, **Water Effects**, **Draw Batching** - **Framerate Cap** — 40, 45 and 50 added (40 divides 120 Hz, 45 divides 90 Hz) - **FPS Percentiles** — the 1% low and p95/p99 next to the average (darchap's, see Credit). Known limitation on the three population cuts: they remove the bodies, not the gameplay objects behind them, so you may still hear pedestrians, traffic and other skaters you cannot see. Being worked on. The average is exactly the statistic that hides a stutter: a steady 60 and a 60 that drops four frames a second read the same. ## Two changed defaults on iOS - **Draw distance now ships at Half.** The static world is roughly 750 of the 765 things drawn in a frame, so it is the only content lever with real weight behind it. Adjust them with `touch_controls`, `touch_controls_opacity` and `touch_haptics` in `mc360.toml`. - **Save thumbnails**: your worlds now show a picture in the world list. - **Exit Game** now closes the app instead of leaving a black screen. ### Performance - Much lower CPU load while playing. The game's threads no longer queue up on a shared lock, calls inside the game run directly, and waits end as soon as the GPU is ready instead of sleeping in whole milliseconds. - Frame rate capped at a steady, evenly paced 60 FPS (`framerate_limit`, default 60). - The game's main thread and GPU thread now get priority on the iPhone's performance cores. - Less heat: the game no longer spins a core at full power while waiting for the GPU, and no longer copies the whole screen image back and forth several times per frame. ### Fixes - Fixed random crashes after playing for a while. - Fixed choppy audio. - Fixed "ghost" blocks and old terrain showing where the world had changed. - Devices with 3 GB of RAM now show an explanation at launch instead of crashing. ### Known issues - Long sessions heat the phone, and iOS then slows it down, so the frame rate can drop over time. Playing unplugged and without a case helps. - The on-screen D-pad's up arrow sits over the first world's thumbnail in the Load menu. It's part of the controls, not the save. - Devices with 3 GB of RAM (iPhone 8 Plus, iPhone X, iPad 8th gen) can't run the game with a normal sideload. They need TrollStore, or a signing method that grants the Extended Virtual Addressing entitlement. Installing over 1.0 keeps your worlds and settings.

# DukeX v1.0.2 - Expanding the Xbox Experience DukeX v1.0.2 is our biggest step yet toward preserving the full original Xbox experience, not just the games. This release introduces the first native macOS build, expands XB.Live integration, and brings richer community features to both iOS and macOS. ## What's New - Native macOS release: DukeX is now available as a Mac Catalyst desktop build packaged with a nested Xemu fork, pairing desktop Xemu compatibility with the DukeX interface. - XB.Live Rich Presence and playtime tracking: friends can see what you are playing while DukeX tracks supported playtime sessions. - XB.Live messaging: threaded conversations, friend messaging, unread indicators, supported game invites, and existing Xbox inbox support now live inside DukeX. - XB.Live social expansion: friend requests, friend management, online presence, and deeper community integration are available from the Profile experience. - Activity Feed: XB.Live news, friend online status, friend achievement unlocks, and community updates now appear in a continuously refreshed timeline. - Controller Landscape Mode: on iOS, compatible controllers can switch DukeX into a controller-first browsing and launch experience. - Expanded AirPlay and external display support: big-screen play is more reliable across supported display configurations. ## Improvements - Improved achievements with Games, Apps, and Cores grouping plus updated artwork handling for XB.Live Core, DukeX Core, and special test titles. - Improved game tile spacing and cover handling across iOS and macOS. - Improved XB.Live cloud-save sync metadata with console identity v2, content-hash dedupe, and server-assisted cross-console restore handling. - Fixed achievement progress rounding so time-based achievements do not show 100% before they are actually complete. ## Availability - iOS: install `DukeX.v1.0.2.ipa` through StikStore, SideStore, or another supported sideloading workflow. - macOS: install `DukeX.macOS.v1.0.2.dmg` by dragging DukeX to Applications. - Hardware requirements on iOS remain Apple A14 Bionic or Apple M1 hardware or newer. - iOS 16.0 or later is supported, with iOS 16 support remaining experimental. ## Important DukeX does not include Xbox system files, game images, BIOS files, copyrighted content, signing certificates, or user games. Users must provide their own legally obtained files. DukeX is intended for legitimate emulation, preservation, testing, and personal library use.

# Iridium 0.2.0 Download your Steam games directly in Iridium, manage repairs and updates, and try the updated Windows runtime. The anonymous ad-hoc carrier alone grants no installation or memory rights. In LiveContainer, the container process's signature, profile, and JIT setup determine effective rights; importing the guest IPA does not grant them. Both routes still need device validation. Back up your saves before updating. Update the existing app or LiveContainer entry without deleting its data. Steam repairs and updates keep older installations; saves stored inside an older game folder may need to be copied manually to the new one. Support still varies by game and device. - **Game prerequisite installers.** Run supported setup steps included with a game, or choose **Game Options → Run Installer** for an EXE or MSI installer you provide. Some installers need interaction. Closing the player requests cancellation; Iridium keeps observing the runtime's exit and reports when a restart is required. - **Reduced duplicate runtime data.** Identical Windows runtime files share one packaged copy. The main app's anonymous ad-hoc signature carries only the increased-memory-limit request; helpers remain unsigned until you sign them. ## Known issues - Physical-device compatibility for these changes has not been established. Some games may fail to launch or have graphics, video, audio, input, save, or shutdown problems. Skyrim speech and mouse attack issues remain unverified. - Keep Iridium open while downloading. Downloads pause when the app goes into the background and need to be resumed. Real-account downloads and recovery after Wi-Fi or network loss still need device testing. - Steam Cloud, Workshop, Steam Families library discovery, password-protected branches, and desktop Steam services are not included. Games that require Steamworks/DRM, anti-cheat, or other unsupported runtime features may not launch after downloading. - Updates keep older game copies and need extra storage. **Download Anyway** does not create free space; exhausting device storage can also prevent other apps from saving. - JIT and available memory depend on your device and signing setup; LiveContainer and standalone results can differ. versions.localizedDescription: # Main changes: - Switched app signing to apple-codesign-quick (the same signer iLoader uses) - Signing is about 6-9x faster - SideInstaller is about 5 MB smaller - Popups that appear together are now merged into one card - The pairing code and its Settings steps are now one popup - An error and its fix steps are now one popup - The "Installed" message, the trust step and LiveContainer's certificate import are now one "Success: last steps" popup - Added clear explanations and steps for more errors - Apple Accounts that are too young to use developer services (error 1102) - Running out of App IDs for the week (error 9120) - Already having 3 apps installed with a free Apple ID - Logging in now automatically retries when Apple temporarily rate limits it (HTTP 429) - Added PanicAnalyzer to the apps that can receive the pairing file ## Fixes: - Fixed LiveContainer + SideStore not downloading while the official LiveContainer GitHub is down (it now uses a temporary mirror, which only has the nightly build) - Fixed imported .ipa files with spaces, symbols or non-Latin letters in their name failing to sign (error 35) - Fixed some imported .ipa files that still had parts of an old signature failing to install - Fixed Side by Side: when two people pair the same iPhone, the second one no longer breaks the first one's pairing - Fixed not being able to revoke "Apple Development" certificates (the ones Xcode makes) in the Certificates tool (error 7252) - Fixed AutoFill filling in the email and password separately on the login page

- Fixed a bug in the installation of the latest nightly of SidesStore - The app would put the pairing file in the wrong path as it has been changed with an update. Issue has been fixed. - Improved visibility of popups

- Messages are now shown as popups to improve clarity - Added advanced options to the install page - Users can now choose the Sidestore (+ Livecontainer) version - Users can now manually import the pairing file on iOS 27+ #60 - Made transitions between pages smoother

Sorry for the instability these days. This update makes SideInstaller fully compatible with the latest releases of all apps, including SideStore Nightly. ## Changes: - SideStore, LiveContainer + SideStore and Feather now accept the pairing file SideInstaller puts in them, instead of asking you for one as though nothing had been placed. SideInstaller now switches on the setting those apps need to reach your iPhone over your local tunnel, which nothing was doing before. - The install may ask you to unlock your iPhone and tap Trust once, and it remembers the result so it won't ask again for that device. If that extra step doesn't work, your install still finishes exactly as it did before, and the log tells you what went out. Pairing tab - One button now writes the pairing file into every supported app it found, instead of you tapping through them one at a time. - One app refusing the pairing file no longer stops the others from getting it. - Export now shares the pairing file that every app can read, so importing it by hand works as well as letting SideInstaller place it.

# Note from the dev V1 is planned to be released by the time that Apple releases iSO 27’s official build. To ensure that, my goal currently is to bring a stable version of the app rather than introducing any new features. This update significantly brings us closer to that goal as it fixes the 2 most common and irritating errors reported so far. Please, keep testing it and share your issues on GitHub or on the discord server. <3 # Changes - Fixed the SideStore nightly error “`Domain=AltSign.Error Code=1 The app extension is missing a valid provisioning profile. UserInfo={NSLocalizedFailureReason =The app extension is missing a valid provisioning profile.}`” - To fix it, the app now writes embedded.mobileprovision into each .appex before sign::sign, and rust-core/Cargo.toml redirects the git dep to it - Fixed a bug that occurred when the app downloaded an .ipa from GitHub - The app now relies on the release’s download link rather than the GitHub API to ensure there are no API cap problems - [Updated dependencies](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FrizzleM/SideInstaller/refs/heads/main/v0.8-dependency-updates.txt)

This update brings significant changes to the backend. The app is now more optimized with LocalDevVPN, which should cause much less issues with tunnel connections being refused or expired. ## Custom IPAs - Users can now import any IPA from Files and SideInstaller signs and installs that instead of downloading. - Documents is now visible in **Files › On My iPhone › SideInstaller**. If you put a SideStore.ipa there, the install uses it. This can be useful for those who cannot access GitHub servers. #9 - A failed download falls back to a copy from an earlier run. - Imports are now backgrounded, work off iCloud Drive, don't destroy the previous file if they fail, and catch a truncated archive at import. ## Security - The pairing file and your signing certificate moved out of Documents to Application Support. This fixes a huge security flaw since apps could abusively access your pairing files without your consent, giving them access to potential security exploits. ## Tunnel and VPN - Any loopback VPN works, not just LocalDevVPN. The UI now says so and names ClashMi too. #9 - A tunnel on a mask other than /24 is detected; a Wi-Fi LAN on the same range no longer reads as a tunnel. - Entering LocalDevVPN's own address in Device IP is caught before the run starts, instead of failing at Connect. - Wi-Fi is only required for pairing. Installing with a saved pairing file works on cellular. ## Fixes - Added new languages, such as Chinese - Pairing tab no longer fails with "adapter closed" after sitting idle, it re-establishes the device link first. - The tunnel/Wi-Fi poll no longer redraws the UI twice a second. - Large builds are mapped rather than read into memory whole during upload. - The activity log is capped at 2000 lines. - Removed the copy button from the code since it can't be pasted into the settings app, meaning it was useless **Full changelog:** https://github.com/FrizzleM/SideInstaller/compare/v0.6.5...v0.7.0

# 3105 1.0.1 Bản cập nhật chính thức tập trung vào Patch workspace v2, trình quản lý Tệp và độ hoàn thiện UI/UX. ## Tính năng mới - Tạo patch bằng cây thư mục theo bundle trong `Trên iPhone của tôi/3105/Patches`; không lưu UUID container. - Tự đồng bộ workspace khi Áp dụng hoặc Xuất, đồng thời tiếp tục hỗ trợ patch v1. - Tự sao lưu file gốc; Khôi phục trả lại file cũ, xóa file patch đã thêm và dọn folder mới sau khi rỗng. - Nhiều tab Tệp độc lập, giữ nguyên vị trí từng tab, chọn nhiều mục, nén ZIP và giải nén ZIP an toàn. - Giao diện iPad split view/landscape, tùy chọn ẩn Dọn dẹp/Hình nền và giao diện nhóm cân đối hơn. - Sửa ô tìm kiếm bị nhấp nháy, tỷ lệ icon/hàng file, CTA trống của Patch và hướng dẫn PosterBoard trên iOS 27. - Bỏ giới hạn cố định cũ về tổng dung lượng payload và số file patch; giới hạn thực tế của thiết bị vẫn áp dụng. ## Hướng dẫn Patch nhanh 1. Tạo cây đường dẫn giống vị trí trong app data và đặt file thay thế vào đó. 4. Quay lại dự án rồi bấm **Áp dụng**; bấm **Khôi phục file gốc** khi muốn hoàn tác. Bạn cũng có thể giữ vào file/folder trong data container và chọn **Tạo patch** để app tự lấy bundle cùng đường dẫn. Xem [hướng dẫn Patch đầy đủ bằng tiếng Việt](https://github.com/YangJiiii/3105/blob/v1.0.1/docs/PATCH_GUIDE.vi.md) hoặc [English guide](https://github.com/YangJiiii/3105/blob/v1.0.1/docs/PATCH_GUIDE.md). ## Cài đặt - Asset đính kèm là IPA **unsigned**, dành để ký lại bằng ESign với chứng chỉ doanh nghiệp. - Bundle đích: `com.apple.mobile.MobileHouseArrest`. - Không hỗ trợ SideStore, AltStore, 3uTools hoặc LiveContainer. - Chỉ dùng trên thiết bị và dữ liệu thuộc sở hữu của bạn; hãy sao lưu trước khi thay đổi app data.

## 3105 1.0 — Bản phát hành chính thức Đây là bản stable đầu tiên của 3105, nâng cấp trực tiếp từ `1.0 beta 3`. ### Có gì mới - **Trình quản lý tệp đầy đủ hơn:** chọn nhiều mục, sao chép, di chuyển, dán, đổi tên, xóa, tạo tệp/thư mục, xem trước, chia sẻ và nén nhiều tệp/thư mục thành ZIP. - **Nhập tệp linh hoạt:** nhập nhiều tệp cùng lúc; khi trùng tên có thể thay thế, giữ cả hai, thay thế tất cả hoặc giữ cả hai cho toàn bộ phiên nhập. - **Patch `.3105`:** bỏ giới hạn nhân tạo về số quy tắc và dung lượng gói/thay thế; đường dẫn vẫn được lưu theo **bundle identifier**, không lưu UUID container của từng máy. - **Mở patch trực tiếp:** hỗ trợ mở tệp `.3105` từ Files và nhập từ website qua liên kết HTTPS `threeoneosfive://import?url=...`. - **Cleaner:** sắp xếp dung lượng từ cao xuống thấp hoặc thấp lên cao; chọn/bỏ chọn tất cả và chọn toàn bộ kết quả đang tìm kiếm. - **Wallpaper Lab:** căn giữa lại nút Áp dụng và giữ giao diện gọn hơn. - **Ngôn ngữ:** các nội dung mới đã được bổ sung cho English, Tiếng Việt và 简体中文. ### Cài đặt - File đính kèm là **IPA chưa ký**, dành cho người dùng tự ký bằng chứng chỉ doanh nghiệp/ESign. - Bundle identifier phải giữ nguyên: `com.apple.mobile.MobileHouseArrest`. - Không hỗ trợ cài qua SideStore, AltStore, 3uTools hoặc LiveContainer. ### An toàn dữ liệu - Hãy sao lưu trước khi sửa dữ liệu ứng dụng. - Cleaner chỉ xóa nội dung trong `Library/Caches` và `tmp` của ứng dụng đã chọn, sau khi người dùng xác nhận. - Patch nhập từ website được tải qua HTTPS, kiểm tra định dạng trước khi lưu và không tự động áp dụng. --- ## English summary 3105 1.0 adds multi-select file operations, preview/share and ZIP creation, conflict-aware multi-file import, uncapped `.3105` patch projects, direct Files/HTTPS website imports, Cleaner size sorting and bulk selection, and updated English/Vietnamese/Simplified Chinese localization. The attached IPA is unsigned and intended for enterprise-certificate/ESign signing. Keep the bundle identifier as `com.apple.mobile.MobileHouseArrest`.

EoL Notice

PancakeStore is officially EoL (End-of-Life) as of 8/22/2026.

Apple has implemented server-side changes to the iTunes API that's used in PancakeStore, as well as other popular tools such as ipatool, which primarily include SEP-based device attestation. What this means, in short, is that PancakeStore will not work ever again unless someone figures out an alternative route for downgrading apps, or successfully re-implements the attestation logic (both of which are very difficult).

In the event that this occurs, or a new method for downgrading apps is discovered and made, we will update PancakeStore.
Until then, consider the project EoL.

Thank you all for all of your support of this tool, and we apologize that things have to halt like this.

**Frame rate cap** @Henyckma added an FPS cap that limits presentation only. The game and the audio keep running at full speed, so it costs nothing in emulation and gives back battery and heat instead. Targets are 15, 23.976, 29.94, 30, 45, 59.97, 60, 90 and 120, set globally or per game. The gain is biggest at 2x and 3x internal resolution, where the passes it skips cover the most pixels. Selecting 30 FPS used to halve emulation and audio speed, which is fixed, and FPS profiles from earlier builds carry over without losing the cadence you picked. **Crashes and freezes** Fixed a crash in games like Namco Museum 50th Anniversary, which turned out to be an out of bounds write in the virtual memory page protection table. Fixed a freeze in readback heavy scenes with Hardware Download Mode set to Unsynchronized. Rogue Galaxy no longer stalls the graphics thread around 7.5 ms every frame on a depth probe readback, about a fifth of the frame on an M2. The last two are bmdhacks. Saving per game settings could also leave the game frozen a second or two later, which is covered below. **Sprite hacks** Align Sprite and Merge Sprite apply when you switch them off. This was the third report of that bug and the fifth attempt at it, and the earlier ones all fixed the global screen while leaving everything around it alone. Per game, those rows greyed out whenever GameDB Graphics Fixes was on, kept showing their old value, and got written back on every save. Align Sprite, Merge Sprite and Wild Arms Offset are one Use Global / Off / On picker each now, and they no longer need manual hacks mode. Setting one claims that fix, so the game database stops overriding it while keeping every other fix for the game. Texture Inside RT, Native Scaling, Bilinear Upscale, Unscaled Palette Draw, Preload Frame Data and Disable Partial Invalidation had the same bug and were fixed with it. None of these do anything at 1x internal resolution, which is by design. **Per-game settings** Turning on Use Per-Game Overrides used to soften text and edges: enabling it copied six graphics keys into the per game file, and one of those forced a blend deinterlace that also suppressed the game's own database fix. Only the settings you change are written now. Saving in that panel could also leave the game frozen a second or two later while the emulator carried on at full speed, because metadata scans share one disc image with the running game and a scan during play left it holding a closed disc. The Renderer picker never saved a change made while a game was running, so it never applied either. It saves now, and it moved from Fixes & Compatibility to the Graphics tab where people kept looking for it. It still applies at the next boot of that game. Saving the panel is quicker too: it used to fire one full settings reload per field written, 71 of them for a single Save. **Settings** Every slider, stepper and typed number is one control now, and each setting is described once instead of once per screen. The FPS target had three different sets of bounds across three screens. Sliders stop on values people actually pick, every stop list holds the default so reset lands on one, and typing still reaches anything in between. Per game numbers can inherit the global value instead of choosing from a short list. The dynamic background sliders stay continuous, since every value there is a legitimate one, but they snap to the precision they print: a row could read 50% while storing 0.4973, which also left the reset arrow comparing against the hidden value. Applying the Default preset asks first and then resets every setting, with the Default row showing as active afterwards, and Reset Graphics and Reset Emulator no longer reach into settings they do not show or drag Frame Pacing to Custom on the way. Buffer Size and Output Latency are sliders on Frame Pacing now, matching the Audio screen, and GS Back Thread says it needs a restart instead of looking broken. The preset fixes are @Henyckma's. **

2.5.1 is mostly a fixes release. The two biggest issues were A12 devices crashing on launch and rumble being completely broken since 2.4.1. Both are fixed, along with a proper no-JIT fallback, several performance improvements, and a collection of Virtual Pad and interface fixes. ## Highlights * Fixed launch crashes on A12 devices * Controller and phone rumble work again * Added improved phone rumble with separate motor handling and a strength setting — @Henyckma * Added a proper no-JIT fallback and improved interpreter performance — @Henyckma * Fixed a Devil May Cry crash during FMVs * Added fractional Internal Resolution options up to 3.5x * Reduced graphics overhead in several games — @bmdhacks * Improved Rogue Galaxy performance — @bmdhacks * Virtual Pad and layout improvements — @Henyckma * GameDB and cheat-loading fixes — @jpolo1224 ## A12 Devices Fixed launch crashes on iPhone XS, XS Max, XR, iPad Air 3, iPad mini 5, iPad 8 and A12X/A12Z iPad Pro. 2.5.0 was accidentally built with an Apple M1 CPU baseline. iOS now targets `apple-a12`, the oldest device we support. ## Rumble Controller and phone rumble work again after being broken since 2.4.1. @Henyckma also reworked phone rumble. It is now sustained, responds properly to motor strength, handles the two PS2 motors separately, and ramps in and out more naturally. A Phone Rumble Strength setting has been added, and Test Rumble now works without a controller connected. Several controller-rumble bugs were fixed at the same time, including a leak, a threading issue and cases where rumble could be routed to the wrong player. ## Playing Without JIT @Henyckma added a proper fallback for devices where JIT is unavailable. Instead of crashing or showing a black screen, ARMSX2 now falls back to interpreter implementations where possible. Interpreter performance was improved at the same time. On the test device and workload, EE time went from 37.55 ms to 30.55 ms, about 18.6% less. Results vary by game, device and thermal state. ## Crashes and Stability Fixed a Devil May Cry crash when the game switches to the software renderer for FMVs. Several related JIT and software-renderer stability issues were fixed as well, including problems affecting legacy JIT mode under LiveContainer. Fastmem now stays disabled correctly when its required 4 GB virtual mapping cannot be allocated, and a race in the JIT keepalive path was narrowed. ## Graphics and Performance @bmdhacks reduced unnecessary render-pass and copy work. Across a five-loop replay: * Rogue Galaxy: 2,411 → 1,741 render passes * OutRun 2006: 1,240 → 1,118 render passes Vertex processing was also reduced in cases where an auto-flush cannot occur. Dragon Quest VIII measured 4.7% fewer graphics-thread cycles in testing. Internal Resolution now includes: `1.25x`, `1.5x`, `1.75x`, `2.25x`, `2.5x`, `2.75x` and `3.5x` ## Game Database @bmdhacks improved Rogue Galaxy performance by disabling auto-flush for the game. Render passes fall 38% and texture copies 74%, worth about 1.8 ms per frame and 2.6 fps on a low-end device. There is a small visual trade-off: some lamp lighting can appear slightly brighter and warmer than the software renderer reference. Four side-by-side comparisons at 1:1 failed to distinguish the two, but please report it if you notice it during normal play. Need for Speed Underground 1 and 2 now run without hardware readbacks — @jpolo1224. ARMSX2 2.5.0 is a major update to the emulator core and the iOS frontend. The biggest core change is a new shared ARM64 recompiler, replacing the older iOS-specific EE, IOP and VU recompilers. It brings iOS in line with the ARM handheld builds, reduces CPU overhead in several parts of emulation, and restores features the previous iOS backend did not support correctly. The release also moves iOS onto the shared game database used by the other mobile ARM builds. That brings a large set of newer per-game fixes and tuning to iOS. Outside the core, 2.5.0 adds Dynamic Controls, animated backgrounds, settings presets, improved frame pacing, proper 120 Hz support, an in-app controller-skin browser, RetroAchievements fixes, OSD improvements, and a long list of graphics and stability fixes. Almost none of this is my own work. The core belongs to @bmdhacks, the new iOS interface and control features to @Henyckma, and the rest to @pstef, @jpolo1224, @XDarkFallenX and Mart. Thanks to all of them, and to everyone who tested development builds and reported problems. ## Highlights * New shared ARM64 recompiler for the EE, IOP and vector units, from @bmdhacks * Updated shared game database with newer fixes and tuning for more than a thousand games * Dynamic Thumbsticks, Swipe Camera, Gyroscope Camera and Dynamic Actions, from @Henyckma * Twelve Metal-rendered Dynamic Background styles, from @Henyckma * Six settings presets plus import and export, from @Henyckma * Emulation-Only Mode, which frees the device to the emulator once a game is running, from @Henyckma * Reworked frame-pacing controls and per-game presets * Proper 120 Hz support on ProMotion devices * Apple GPU fixes for speckled graphics in games such as Black and God of War II, from @bmdhacks * Fixes for upscaling hacks and settings that previously appeared not to apply * In-app controller-skin browser and more reliable skin importing * Working RetroAchievements statistics, achievement lists and native notifications * OSD safe-area, rotation and performance-overlay fixes * Several iOS crashes and core correctness bugs fixed ## New ARM64 Recompiler ARMSX2 now uses the newer shared ARM64 recompiler family written by @bmdhacks and tested primarily on ARM handheld hardware, replacing the older iOS-specific implementations. The new backend has had considerably more testing, including differential tests that compare recompiled EE, IOP and VU execution against other emulator implementations. It also contains substantial optimization work around register handling, larger compiled blocks, vector instructions, calls and returns, unaligned memory accesses, and self-modifying code. Several features that were missing from the previous iOS backend are also supported now: * Dynamic game patches can be applied from the game database. Entries such as the ones used by Armored Core: Nine Breaker and Ratchet & Clank 2 previously had no effect on iOS. * Goemon's TLB handling now has the required preload and invalidation hooks. The fix remains behind the existing game fix and would still benefit from a complete playthrough test. * Delay-slot swapping is supported where the PS2 allows it. The JIT has also been adapted to the different executable-memory paths used by the app, including the iOS 26 TXM paths, Simulator support, and the legacy path used on iOS 18 and earlier. ## Game Compatibility iOS no longer ships its own separate merged game database. ARMSX2 now uses the shared database. The move onto the shared resources was done by @bmdhacks. The previous iOS copy had fallen behind upstream. With the shared database, more than a thousand games have different behavioral entries compared with 2.4.1, and future mobile fixes no longer need to be copied separately into the iOS version. Some of the more visible changes include: * Hardware-readback tuning is now actually applied from the game database, thanks to @jpolo1224 making the database key work at all. Forty-eight games currently use it, including Black,

Game is now playable, although one graphical issue remains from my testing. Folder memory cards work on a custom data folder again. Creating save data crashed or reported "format failed" for anyone whose data folder wasn't internal app storage. Texture Packs: Importing a pack no longer freezes the app when using an SD card. A real pack is thousands of files over SAF, and the copy ran on the UI thread, black screen, then "ARMSX2 isn't responding", worse on SD. Import and delete now run in the background with a live file count to let you know when it's completed. BC/DXT packs work on GPUs without hardware support. Patches work with RetroAchievements Hardcore enabled again. ARMSX2 iOS 2.4.1 is a much bigger follow-up than the version number might suggest. This update adds video library backgrounds, MetalFX upscaling, more flexible controller and RetroAchievements settings, save-state previews, and a long list of interface improvements. There has also been a lot of work under the hood. JIT handling is more resilient, several ARM64 and Metal paths have been improved, and a number of game-specific compatibility problems have been fixed. Thank you to everyone who tested the builds, reported issues, and kept checking the fixes. ## Library backgrounds Library backgrounds have been rebuilt around separate portrait and landscape slots. Setting a portrait background no longer replaces the landscape one, or vice versa. Each slot clearly shows its orientation, file type, and size, so it is easier to see exactly what you are editing. Each orientation also has its own fit mode: * **Fill** fills the screen and crops the edges when necessary. * **Fit** keeps the entire image visible and may add letterboxing. * **Stretch** fills the screen by changing the image proportions. Stretch mode has been fixed so it no longer leaves black bars along the sides in portrait or at the top and bottom in landscape. Alongside static and animated images, the library can now use looping video backgrounds. MP4, MKV, and WebM files can be selected, and the player swaps cleanly when a different video is chosen. Videos resume properly after returning to the app and pause while ARMSX2 is in the background. Background importing is also safer. A failed import can no longer remove or replace the background you were already using. The dimming control now shows a live percentage, making it easier to use the same intensity across different backgrounds. ## Game cards Portrait game cards finally receive the same frosted-glass treatment as their landscape versions. A subtle gradient behind the cards gives the glass something consistent to blur, while Reduce Transparency users receive an opaque fallback. The cards themselves have received a small layout pass: * Titles, file information, size, and region are centered beneath the cover. * Additional padding gives the contents more breathing room. * The favorite star has a lighter and less distracting background. * The BIOS Only button is easier to notice. * Favorite buttons in the list view have a larger and more reliable tap area. ## Save states and memory cards Save states now display the screenshot captured with each state. This should make it much easier to recognise the point in the game you are about to restore. Memory cards can be exported through the standard iOS share sheet. ZIP archives containing memory cards can also be imported directly into the app. ## Gameplay and controls Portrait gameplay uses more of the available screen. The game viewport has been increased from 55% to 60% of the screen height, reducing the unused space between the game and the virtual controller. The in-game pause button now uses a proper pause symbol instead of the previous ellipsis icon. The menu button also has better contrast, helping it remain visible over bright game scenes. ARMSX2 now keeps the display awake while a game is running. ### Stick inversion Each virtual stick axis can be inverted independently: * Left stick horizontal * Left stick vertical * Right stick horizontal * Right stick vertical These options have global defaults and can also be overridden for individual games. The on-screen stick still follows your finger normally; only the input sent to the game is inverted. ### Rumble and haptics When no rumble-capable physical controller is connected, PS2 rumble events can now be translated into iPhone haptic feedback. This respects the existing Haptic Feedback setting and is rate-limited so sustained rumble does not overload the device’s haptic engine. ## Pause menu Long game titles use end truncation instead of cutting text out of the middle, which keeps the beginning of the title readable. ARMSX2 2.6.0.5 What's new: Gyro + stick now work together. Aim gyro (and steering gyro) is now added on top of the physical stick instead of fighting it, use the right stick for coarse aim and tilt to fine-tune, both at once. The other stick (movement) is unaffected while you aim. Fixed: per-game stick fixes leaked to every game. Right/Left Stick Invert X/Y, Swap X/Y, and D-pad as Left Stick now save per game when set in a game's properties (they were writing the global setting for all games). Added Per-game BIOS option. The patch/cheat browser reads the game's serial straight from the disc, so you can browse and install patches from a game's per-game settings without booting it first (previously it only worked in-game). ANGLE is now an OpenGL driver option. When you select the OpenGL renderer, the driver picker shows an ANGLE option (GLES-on-Vulkan), the OpenGL counterpart to the Vulkan driver list. Helps non-Adreno GPUs (Mali/Xclipse/PowerVR) whose native OpenGL driver is weak. Available in both the Renderer settings and the in-game Graphics menu.
